response.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS test_count FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), totals AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) AS average_count, SUM(test_count) AS total_count FROM sex_counts) SELECT sc.sex, sc.test_count, CAST(sc.test_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS fraction_of_total, sc.test_count - t.average_count AS above_average FROM sex_counts AS sc CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE sc.test_count > t.average_count

assumptions.assumption: The fraction uses the total test count across all sex groups, including groups whose counts are not above average.

alternatives.interpretation: The fraction uses only the total test count across the above-average sex groups shown.
alternatives.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS test_count FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), average_count AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) AS value FROM sex_counts), qualifying AS (SELECT sc.sex, sc.test_count, sc.test_count - a.value AS above_average FROM sex_counts AS sc CROSS JOIN average_count AS a WHERE sc.test_count > a.value) SELECT sex, test_count, CAST(test_count AS REAL) / SUM(test_count) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, above_average FROM qualifying
